q1: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q2: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY CUSTOMER_ID HAVING SUM(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT SUM(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY CUSTOMER_ID HAVING SUM(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT SUM(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
counterexample: INSERT INTO PRODUCT (PRODUCT_KEY) VALUES (1), (2), (3); INSERT INTO CUSTOMER (CUSTOMER_ID, PRODUCT_KEY) VALUES (1, 1), (1, 2), (1, 3), (2, NULL);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent. Q1 checks if the number of distinct products a customer has purchased is equal to the total number of distinct products in the database. Q2 checks if the sum of distinct product keys for a customer is equal to the sum of distinct product keys in the product table. These are fundamentally different conditions.
counterexample_dsp: A customer has purchased all products, and another customer has purchased no products.
